messages:
alex_sales: Quick sync — POC with AcmeCorp. They want Redwood Private. Need network checklist: peering vs PrivateLink, required CIDRs, subnets, route tables, SGs, test steps. Can someone outline minimal ask we pass to customer? Thanks :pray:

sam_sre: Recommend PrivateLink for cross-account w/ least privilege and no route table changes. VPC Peering ok if both VPCs are same org/region and they want L3 access. Key items: non-overlapping CIDRs, 2 AZ subnets for endpoints/ENIs, security group rules, NAT for outbound telemetry. Quick list below.

maria_eng: +1 on PrivateLink for security. If they want friendly hostnames (eg api.redwood.internal) enable private DNS on the endpoint.

sam_sre: Minimal VPC peering config:
```
- Customer VPC CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16
- Redwood VPC CIDR: 10.20.0.0/16
- Create VPC Peering connection (same region)
- Add route table entry in customer RT: 10.20.0.0/16 -> pcx-0123456789abcdef
- Add route table entry in redwood RT: 10.10.0.0/16 -> pcx-0123456789abcdef
- Update SGs to allow TCP 443 from peer CIDR
- Note: no transitive routing; can't route peered traffic to VPNs/other VPCs
```

jordan_se: For PrivateLink (recommended for POCs across accounts):
```
- We expose an Interface Endpoint Service (com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-xxxxx)
- Customer creates Interface Endpoints in 1 subnet per AZ (private subnets preferred)
- Subnet IDs: <subnet-az1>, <subnet-az2> (we need these)
- Security Group: allow inbound TCP 443 from customer app subnets / SG
- Enable 'Private DNS' option if they want to resolve our hostname automatically
- We give them service name and accept endpoint connection (or auto-accept for known accounts)
```

alex_sales: Ports? Any extra firewall rules? Also what do they need to give us (ARNs, subnet IDs, KMS key)?

sam_sre: Minimum ports: TCP 443. If they want outbound telemetry/health to our SaaS, allow HTTPS outbound to our telemetry IP ranges (we'll provide a list). No SSH. For peering: ensure route table entries exist both ways. For PrivateLink: SG must allow inbound 443 from the consumer. We will need: subnet IDs (one private per AZ), security group id to allow the endpoint ENIs (or permission to create one), and confirmation that their VPC CIDR does not overlap with 10.20.0.0/16. If they require customer-managed KMS for data at rest, they must add a KMS key policy grant for our account/service principal (include account id).

maria_eng: Test steps to validate connectivity:
```
1) From customer app host: curl -v https://<endpoint-hostname>/health
2) nc -vz <endpoint-ip> 443
3) traceroute <endpoint-ip> (peering will show direct hop to peer)
```

alex_sales: Cool. Can we send this as a one-pager to customer? I'll include the sample route table and test commands. Any docs link?

deploy-bot: Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/private-vpc-setup (internal) :link:

sam_sre: I'll draft and DM you a concise checklist. Also note: if customer uses overlapping CIDRs we recommend either re-IP or use a VPN + NAT; peering can't handle overlap. :warning:

jordan_se: FYI — for Dedicated GPU pools in the customer's VPC we typically only need routing entries and SGs; PrivateLink is mainly for cross-account control plane/private endpoints.

alex_sales: Thanks all! I'll send to Acme and follow up with subnet IDs by EOD. :thumbsup:
